approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a SELFIES variational autoencoder on the permitted unlabeled corpus and freezes it. A complete Gaussian state contains both the semantic latent and the variables that determine categorical decoding, so each state produces one reproducible molecule. During an objective, a Gaussian process learns from the fingerprints and scores of that session's accepted molecules. Parallel pCN chains sample the Gaussian prior weighted by the GP probability of beating the best observed score. The Parent randomly takes a novel batch from retained chain states and submits the exact molecules used for prediction.
approach.novelty: Add empirical elite-threshold conditioning: after each feedback message, use the 90th percentile of accepted scores as the probability threshold. This asks whether a molecule can enter the observed upper score region even when an isolated record lies far above the decoder's predicted scores. The proposed causal change is a less extreme threshold that changes which pCN transitions are accepted. This lineage has only its root so far; its incumbent threshold is the direct comparator, and no sibling has tried an elite-percentile threshold.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-a08278654dda has a single screening-seed macro score of 0.433166996019497; the supplied aggregate is incomplete and supplies no multi-seed reliability estimate. Its actual summary.json and run.log show successful completion with 1450 valid unique proposals. Its Curate evidence confirms moving chains and positive retained-minus-prior log incumbent-improvement probability on all five tasks. Nevertheless, joining each saved submitted prediction to the preceding accepted trajectory shows that every one of the 280 submissions in rounds 2 through 29 on drd2_docking, and every one of the corresponding 280 on sitagliptin_mpo, has (posterior_mean - current_incumbent)/posterior_std below -3. In the last round the mean standardized deficits are 9.903798 and 6.956466 respectively. The last-round observed 90th percentiles are 0.067806 and 0.025240, while the incumbents are 0.867722 and 0.212429. The behavior being addressed is conditioning on a record far outside the decoder's predicted score region. Small absolute probabilities are not evidence of numerical underflow or absent steering: the Parent computes log_ndtr and its probabilities vary. Whether this extreme threshold harms score discovery is the hypothesis, not an established causal conclusion. The supplied mechanism-cluster view is empty, and the immutable Parent observation contains no earlier elite-threshold attempt.
hypothesis: Replace the observed-maximum threshold in the Parent's GP-probability pCN target with the linearly interpolated empirical 90th percentile of unique accepted current-session scores, so the same prior-preserving sampler conditions on entering an observed elite score region instead of exceeding an isolated incumbent.

finding_summary.headline: Elite conditioning changed sampling but lowered the single-seed mean score to 0.391
finding_summary.insights:
An extreme incumbent tail can be relaxed enough to materially redirect sampling without improving record discovery. The paired receipts rule out an inactive cutoff, unaccepted labels or prediction/submission mismatch as explanations for this score result. Lowering the cutoff changed relative preferences: it accepted 5,401 moves the incumbent rule would reject, and rejected 1,103 moves that rule would accept. The effect therefore includes which molecular transitions are preferred, as well as the overall acceptance rate.

On the two sessions that motivated the intervention, the elite target became permissive: mean retained-minus-prior log elite probability was only 0.087 for drd2_docking and 0.021 for sitagliptin_mpo. Their scores moved in opposite directions. This narrows the next question to how much record-seeking pressure is useful, and whether the GP can distinguish useful molecular arrangements within the decoder's reachable space. The molecular assessment finds abundant rings and familiar medicinal fragments, but inconsistent whole-molecule assembly and control of functional-group placement in both runs; threshold relaxation leaves those generator limitations open. These chemistry observations suggest further hypotheses, not a proven cause of the score loss. One seed establishes the logged behavioral effect but cannot establish the reliability of the score tradeoff, GP calibration or equilibrium mixing.
finding_summary.results:
The intended threshold and sampling effects occurred. All 145 fitted cutoffs exactly matched the accepted-score 90th percentile and lay below the incumbent. On 4,640 identical prior probes, the mean standardized threshold deficit fell from 5.193 to 1.057, and the fraction more than three posterior standard deviations below the cutoff fell from 66.49% to 0.43%. Retained states showed the same direction in every round. Replaying both rules with the same proposals and random draws changed 6,504 of 36,800 accept/reject decisions (17.67%); every actual update followed the elite rule. All 1,450 submitted molecules retained exact prediction identity and filled the budget.

The seed-0 mean final-best score fell from 0.433167 to 0.390832, a decrease of 0.042335. The largest change was drd2_docking, which fell from 0.867722 to 0.572905. median_2 fell from 0.171784 to 0.167839. Gains on zaleplon_mpo (0.340635 to 0.375713), deco_hop (0.573265 to 0.574331) and sitagliptin_mpo (0.212429 to 0.263373) did not offset those losses. This is confirmed mechanism activation with a negative score result on the one available seed.

molecular.headline: Abundant rings and medicinal fragments coexist with awkward connectivity and no defined stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment covers every supplied objective for seed 0: each digest contains 300 evaluated structures, including 290 optimizer proposals. The output is structurally broad, spanning ordinary aryl heterocycles, saturated amine rings, fused and bridged systems, lactams, ethers and esters, alongside long polyenes and unusually connected nitrogen, sulfur and phosphorus groups. Most molecules have a substantial medicinal-chemistry-sized skeleton, but very small fragments and much larger, highly decorated structures also occur. Ring chemistry is abundant: the per-task ring_closure_rate spans 0.9828 to 0.9966, and aromatic_atom_rate spans 0.7793 to 0.8897. These are SMILES presence rates, not perceived ring counts or fractions of atoms that are aromatic. Mean SMILES lengths span 44.6 to 46.4; text length is not molecular weight. Every stereocentre_rate is 0.0 despite structures containing potentially stereogenic tetrahedral centres. The lack of stereochemical specification does not imply that all structures are planar. The parent trajectories show the same broad mixture of recognizable fragments and awkward assemblies. There are chemically interpretable individual proposals, but broad structural diversity and accepted SMILES do not establish a feasible synthesis, an ordinary closed-shell state, or stability. Score-gradient readings below are associations within these trajectories; they do not identify hidden target structures or prove that any particular functional group caused a score.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring proposals are mostly moderately sized ring assemblies with aromatic carbon, ring nitrogen or oxygen, and limited peripheral substitution. Evaluation 149, score 0.37571328785207686, joins a fused N-methyl N/O aromatic system to an alcohol-bearing side chain and a fluorinated unsaturated aza ring with an amino substituent. Evaluation 185, score 0.33690534619560325, is a much more conventional methylimidazole bearing benzyl and chlorobenzyl-thioether substituents. The initial trimethoxyindole carboxamide at evaluation 9 already scores 0.3051048083696145. The low end includes an extensively benzylated, peptide-like amide assembly with unusual sulfur at evaluation 11 and a large polyunsaturated ring assembly at evaluation 179. The late set still mixes exotic phosphorus/sulfur structures with the aryl-thiophene thioamide and unsaturated lactone at evaluation 299. Synthetic plausibility is therefore mixed rather than uniformly poor.
liabilities: The high-scoring fused imine structure at evaluation 110 includes a small, densely connected nitrogen ring; several other high structures also have unusual unsaturated ring closures that complicate a plausible synthesis.

Evaluations 223 and 268 carry conjugated aldehyde substituents. Evaluation 299 combines an aldehyde, thioamide and unsaturated lactone, so a useful score does not remove potential chemical reactivity.
The late phosphorus species at evaluation 295 and bracketed hydrogen-bearing sulfur at evaluation 296 are unusual valence environments for an ordinary medicinal series.
missing_features: The set lacks consistent elaboration of the compact, chemically conventional heteroaromatic arrangements already represented by the imidazole and initial indole carboxamide; many alternatives change ring topology and appendage size at the same time.

No uniquely required absent functional group can be inferred. The evident gap is reproducible control of scaffold size and substituent polarity, rather than absence of rings, nitrogen, carbonyls or halogens.
Configurations are unspecified at the alcohol-bearing and other tetrahedral centres; the trajectory provides no stereochemical comparison from which to infer a preferred configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best score is 0.37571328785207686 and the digest median is 0.011458. The larger, flexible amide-rich structure at evaluation 11 scores 4.062031856671369e-45, while evaluation 179 scores 9.963756221572277e-36. Together with the high aromatic examples, this supports a preference for a bounded scaffold size and a coherent aromatic/heteroatom arrangement over indiscriminate molecular growth. Smallness alone is insufficient: the initial alkyl bromide scores 8.305895500294491e-10. Carbonyls are not an established requirement because the best proposal lacks one. The fluoro/chloro matched pair at evaluations 223 and 268 has the identical score 0.3365357296869613, so halogen identity is not a differentiating signal in that pair. Parent n-a08278654dda reaches 0.340634631669846 with an aryl-substituted diazacycle bearing a small N/O ring; the child maximum has a more fused aromatic core, while the parent and child share the 0.33966649739182625 sulfur-containing heterocycle at evaluation 111. The higher maximum does not coincide with removal of questionable ring connectivity.

per_task.generated_character: The upper end is rich in aromatic and heteroaromatic rings with multiple nitrogen functions, usually on moderately sized to larger scaffolds. Evaluation 247, score 0.5743310208126858, contains linked and fused aza-aromatic systems joined through an extended unsaturated N-N-containing segment. Evaluation 253, score 0.5664592760180995, has a recognizable aryl amide and indole, but its intervening carbon also bears a nitroso group. Evaluation 191 combines a biphenyl amide with imine/hydrazone chemistry, while evaluation 218 combines an aryl amide, a saturated diazacycle, a thiourea and a fused N/O heteroaromatic ring. Familiar synthetic fragments are present, but the output does not define a consistently straightforward series. The low examples include unsaturated sulfone-linked rings, a saturated cyclic sulfone with a fused N/O ring system, and the morpholine-containing sulfone at evaluation 299.
liabilities: Nitroso substitution at evaluation 253, extended imine/hydrazone connectivity at evaluations 247 and 191, and the allyl thioether/thiourea combination at evaluation 218 warrant chemical scrutiny before treating these as ordinary stable analogues.

The final evaluation-296 structure has a very elaborate polycyclic assembly containing bracketed hydrogen-bearing sulfur, ester/amide groups and a carboxylic acid; a recognizable morpholine appendage does not make the full assembly straightforward to synthesize.
missing_features: The upper structures suggest value in specific aromatic nitrogen and donor/acceptor arrangements, but systematic chemically stable versions of those arrangements are missing from the bounded high-scoring set.

The evidence cannot identify a missing target decoration or a required scaffold replacement: broad structural classes already overlap in score, and the apparent sulfone association has a strong parent counterexample.
Defined stereochemistry is absent even in substituted indole side chains and saturated fused systems.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The digest median is 0.520459. Aromatic nitrogen-containing assemblies at evaluations 247, 191 and 158 sit above the nonaromatic or less aromatic sulfone-rich structures at evaluations 50, 170 and 299, whose scores are 0.25758568374594853, 0.26375771547557075 and 0.26539368531376917. Yet the tiny propionitrile at evaluation 41 still scores 0.5, and the extended polyene/amide structure at evaluation 99 scores 0.5609057782404998. Thus the narrow upper score differences do not establish a general size penalty, and the low sulfone examples do not establish that sulfones themselves are disfavored. In fact, parent n-a08278654dda's maximum, 0.5732649174777824 at evaluation 218, is an aryl sulfone attached to a nitrogen-rich heterocyclic assembly. The child maximum replaces that chemistry with a more extensively conjugated aza-ring assembly, without a clear improvement in apparent synthetic plausibility. The shared evaluation-158 structure scores 0.5644679320458192 in both trajectories.

per_task.generated_character: The useful upper examples combine aromatic surfaces with nitrogen-containing linkers or saturated nitrogen rings. Evaluation 87, score 0.572904722089471, is an arylpiperazine connected to an N-hydroxy, unsaturated amino fragment and a phosphine-substituted phenyl group. Evaluation 29, score 0.31273900914359654, carries a dimethylaminopropylamino chain on a methoxybenzene fused to an unsaturated four-membered carbocycle; the small ring is chemically consequential. Evaluation 18 contains a tetrahydroisoquinoline-like tertiary amine, and evaluation 135 combines a secondary amino linker, an aryl ether, a pyridine and an oxime. The low end contains aryl imines, amides, conjugated nitrogen systems and thioethers without an equivalent exposed saturated amine arrangement. The overall output still spans small fragments, ordinary medium-sized scaffolds and much larger polyunsaturated assemblies.
liabilities: The best proposal contains an arylphosphine and an N-hydroxy unsaturated amino unit. Their possible chemical liabilities are separate from the supplied score.

Evaluation 29 has an unusual fused unsaturated four-membered ring; evaluation 255 adds a pyridinium group and an amino carbon attached to pyrrolidine, giving a different charge and aminal environment from a simple tertiary amine.
Hydrazone-like connectivity, nitro groups and extended unsaturation remain in late proposals; the broad output does not establish a stable or synthetically coherent amine series.
missing_features: Reliable construction of accessible aliphatic amine centres at controlled positions relative to aromatic surfaces is underdeveloped. Such centres are present, so this is a problem of their arrangement and recurrence, not absolute absence.

Chemically uncomplicated versions of the useful aryl/amine arrangements are not consistently represented among the strongest child examples: phosphine, N-O, oxime and unusual small-ring features accompany them.

The observed cationic or nitrogen-rich structures do not by themselves specify a useful protonation state; amide, imine, aromatic and saturated amine nitrogen must remain chemically distinct in this reading.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best score is 0.572904722089471, but the digest median is 0.007702. The amine-bearing structures at evaluations 29, 18 and 135 score 0.31273900914359654, 0.2586499693063822 and 0.21811628298646404, whereas the aryl imine at evaluation 212 scores 0.00011879516001877162 and the simple phenoxypropyl amide at evaluation 55 scores 0.00033303319833196673. This supports an association with the chemical state and placement of nitrogen near aromatic groups, rather than nitrogen count alone. It is not sufficient: the final N-N-linked diazacycle at evaluation 299 scores only 0.0014980745212506842. Parent n-a08278654dda's strongest structure at evaluation 208, score 0.8677224451996757, combines an aminopropyl group and a tertiary cyclic amine with benzene, ether and thiophene elements; its evaluation-267 structure, score 0.7993263925636829, also has saturated aliphatic amines. The child retains individual amine-bearing hits, including the shared 0.31273900914359654 structure, but its maximum adds unusual phosphine/N-O chemistry and remains below those parent values. No binding pose or measured protonation state was supplied.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger proposals combine multiple rings with carbonyl-containing or ether-containing motifs: lactams, esters, cyclic amide/urea-like units, aryl ethers and oxygenated aromatic rings. Evaluation 257, score 0.16273417606729546, is an elaborate polycyclic amine/imine and lactone assembly with a dihydroxybenzene element. The late evaluation-295 structure, score 0.16095095675340096, is a more compact N-methyl pyrrole fused to a lactam ring, with a phenyl substituent and an oxazoline ring. Evaluation 242 is a benzene-fused medium-ring lactam bearing a methyl ester and benzyl substituent; evaluation 151 is an oxygen-linked aromatic cyclic ketone assembly. The fixed initial structure at evaluation 7 contains a fused nitrogen heterocycle with carbonyls, phenyl substitution and a hydroxybenzoate ester, and remains the highest-scoring structure in the child trajectory. At the other extreme are formaldehyde and a long acyclic brominated polyene containing multiple nitrogen linkages.
liabilities: Evaluation 257 obtains an upper-set score with a complicated bridged ring system and an imine; this is less straightforward medicinal chemistry than its recognizable amine, phenol and ester fragments imply.
The acyclic evaluation-116 structure combines extensive unsaturation, bromination and N-N linkages. Evaluation 80 has adjacent positively charged nitrogen atoms in an unusual ring system.

The final evaluation-296 polycycle remains large and densely connected, with several imine-containing rings; late output is not uniformly represented by the more conventional lactam at evaluation 295.
missing_features: The output lacks consistent preservation and controlled variation of the organized aromatic/heterocyclic and carbonyl/ether arrangements already visible in the initial and stronger generated molecules.
Ring and oxygen atoms are plentiful; the unresolved feature is their specific connectivity and spacing, which the score comparisons cannot reduce to a single required heterocycle or carbonyl count.
Potentially stereogenic benzylic and ring-junction centres, including that in evaluation 295, remain unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial evaluation-7 score is 0.1678386594791329; no child proposal exceeds it. The best generated score is 0.16273417606729546 and the digest median is 0.109215. The low formaldehyde score of 0.008773280079294957 and acyclic polyene score of 0.015539494866471998 contrast with the ring-rich, oxygenated upper structures. The latter low example is not merely too small, supporting an association with organized ring and functional-group topology. Carbonyls are common in the upper set but not obligatory: the aryl-ether/imidazole structure at evaluation 248 scores 0.1566926618156574. Parent n-a08278654dda reaches 0.1717839775079566 with an aromatic, oxygenated polycycle containing several amide carbonyls. The child reproduces the parent's evaluation-260 polycycle at its evaluation 257 with the same 0.16273417606729546 score. This looks like broad coverage of the same oxygenated ring chemistry, with additional unrelated structures rather than evidence for a new missing functional group.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest proposals are moderately sized but chemically varied: an N/O polycyclic amidine connected to an aldehyde-bearing cyclic enol ether at evaluation 182; a vinylpyridine with an oxime ether and thiol/hydrazone segment at evaluation 256; a polyenynyl cationic aza ring attached to an aminopyrazole at evaluation 123; and unsaturated imide/lactone or imide/ether ring systems at evaluations 17 and 77. They are not a coherent conventional amine-amide series. The bottom end includes both heavily decorated large ring assemblies and sprawling chains with multiple phenyl groups, boron or phosphorus, many unsaturated bonds and several polar functions. Familiar functional groups are available, but their combined architectures often look difficult to make and chemically delicate.
liabilities: Evaluation 182 combines an aldehyde, cyclic enol ether and amidine-containing polycycle; evaluation 256 adds oxime-ether, thiol/hydrazone and enol functionality. Their scores do not demonstrate stability or a practical route.

The shared parent/child cationic structure at evaluation 123 contains an undercoordinated bracketed positive nitrogen; direct graph inspection identifies radical character, so it should not be interpreted as an ordinary protonated amine.
The bromomethyl group and multiply unsaturated medium/large rings in evaluation 17, and the very elaborate ring connectivity at evaluation 52, create additional chemical and synthetic concerns.
missing_features: The set lacks a repeatedly expressed, chemically uncomplicated combination of modest scaffold size and organized polar ring/linker functionality; high values are attached to structurally disparate and often delicate assemblies.

No specific absent pharmacophore is supported by these molecules alone. Nitrogen, carbonyls, ethers and halogens all occur among very low structures as well as some higher ones, so their presence cannot identify the missing arrangement.
Defined stereochemistry is absent from the polycyclic and substituted ring structures, but the available scores cannot establish a stereochemical preference.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Evaluation 182 scores 0.26337307291649803 and evaluation 256 scores 0.22480871596011054. They exceed parent n-a08278654dda's maximum, 0.21242900824222632, which belongs to the same cationic polyenynyl/aminopyrazole structure found at child evaluation 123. The higher child maximum therefore has a more oxygenated cyclic amidine/enol-ether arrangement, but still carries an aldehyde and unusual ring connectivity. The very large structures at evaluations 52 and 167 score exactly 0.0, while the benzyl-rich nitrogen-containing structure at evaluation 172 scores 1.5436686042133222e-64. Modest size and an integrated polar arrangement appear more compatible with the upper region than extensive hydrophobic or polyfunctional growth; this is not a clean matched-pair inference. Halogens alone are uninformative: the best proposal is unhalogenated, whereas the multiply fluorinated late evaluation-297 structure scores 2.151807787068372e-13. The digest median is reported as 0.0, but the trajectory includes many tiny nonzero scores, so that rounded median is not an exact-zero count. Late evaluations 299 and 300 remain at 1.981355285913548e-05 and 1.397896131843601e-05 despite amine/heterocycle content.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring and aromatic token presence are high, yet upper examples include ONC(=CCc1ccccc1P)N1CCN(c2ccccc2F)CC1 with phosphine and N-O chemistry, and Cc1cc(OC(F)F)ccc1C(=O)NC(Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)N=O with a nitroso group. More conventional chemistry is demonstrably available in Cc1ncc(SCc2cccc(Cl)c2)n1Cc1ccccc1. The deficit is therefore the reliability of whole-molecule assembly, not absence of useful fragments. Unusual groups occur at both high and low scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably assemble familiar medicinal fragments into chemically uncomplicated, interpretable whole molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs stronger control of functional-group compatibility, ordinary valence/electronic states and ring connectivity while retaining its broad de novo scaffold coverage. It should be able to vary an existing useful arrangement without incidentally adding reactive or exotic groups. This chemical plausibility gap does not justify assuming that every such group universally lowers the score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: COc1cccc2c1C=C2NCCCN(C)C scores 0.31273900914359654, and Cc1ccc(F)cc1OCCNCC(CC=NO)Cc1ccccn1 scores 0.21811628298646404 in their supplied session, whereas CCCC(=O)NCCCOc1ccccc1 scores 0.00033303319833196673 in that same session. The latter still contains nitrogen and an aromatic ether, but its nitrogen is an amide. The corresponding parent's strongest structures also carry saturated aliphatic amines. The child clearly can emit such centres; the missing capability is repeatable control of their attachment and environment, not simple nitrogen enrichment.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve the chemical state and placement of amine nitrogen relative to aromatic surfaces.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator should be able to retain or vary an aliphatic amine centre, its substitution and its spacing from a ring independently of wholesale scaffold changes. Distinguish that chemistry from amides, conjugated imines, aromatic nitrogen and unusual formal charges. Which nitrogen environment to retain must come from current-session observations, without an objective-specific motif rule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Compact organized examples such as Cn1cc(C2=NCCO2)c2c1NC(=O)CC2c1ccccc1 score well relative to the acyclic C=COC(=CC=CC#CCC)NC=NC=C(Br)C=NNN=NC(Br)=CC=O in their shared trajectory. Elsewhere large decorated structures reach tiny scores. However, C=CC=C(C(=O)C=CCNCC=C(CC=C)NC(=O)c1cc(C(C)NCc2cnc(C)[nH]2)ccc1O)c1cccnc1C(C)=NON has recorded scores 0.5609057782404998 and 2.241116085184792e-33 in different sessions. Thus a universal small-molecule or ring-count preference would contradict the evidence. A fluoro/chloro matched pair is present, but most cited upper structures differ by much more than a controlled substituent change.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks reliable independent control of scaffold topology, molecular extent and polar-group placement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support de novo variations that change a substituent or ring connection while preserving the rest of a chemically meaningful size and donor/acceptor arrangement. Molecular growth, contraction and polarity changes should be controllable dimensions whose value is learned from the local scores. Broad ring coverage already exists; simply increasing ring or heteroatom occurrence does not fill this gap.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every supplied proposal-set stereocentre_rate is 0.0. Cn1c2ccccc2c2oc(C(O)CC3=NC=CC(N)C=C3F)cc21 contains an unspecified alcohol-bearing centre, and Cn1cc(C2=NCCO2)c2c1NC(=O)CC2c1ccccc1 contains an unspecified substituted tetrahedral ring carbon. Both appear among the higher-scoring proposals. This is absent stereochemical specification, not proof of absent three-dimensional shape or proof that a particular enantiomer would score better.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces potentially stereogenic structures without representing defined tetrahedral configurations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs the capacity to retain and deliberately vary valid explicit stereochemical assignments when its scaffolds create stereogenic centres. No preferred configuration can be prescribed from these trajectories; any utility would have to be established from permitted current-session feedback.

method_name: COWBOYS: GP-conditioned de novo latent sampling
method_thesis: Train a compact SELFIES VAE from the permitted unlabeled corpus during preparation, then freeze its decoder. Within each independent objective session, fit a Tanimoto-kernel GP directly to the observed molecular fingerprints and scores. Generate new molecules through preconditioned Crank-Nicolson MCMC targeting the Gaussian latent prior multiplied by the GP probability that the deterministically decoded molecule exceeds the observed incumbent. The molecule assessed by the surrogate must be the molecule submitted. Fill the protocol-announced batch with distinct generated structures and update the GP after feedback. The corpus supplies a generative prior, never a ranked molecule library. This follows the decoupled mechanism in [COWBOYS](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/moss25a.html). Our hypothesis is that structure-level prediction and immediate Bayesian conditioning can direct scarce labels toward a higher final observed maximum without fitting a reward-dependent neural generator. Success is measured by the benchmark's mean of independent final Top-1 scores.

method_references.title: Moss, H., Ober, S. W., and Diethe, T. Return of the Latent Space COWBOYS: Re-thinking the use of VAEs for Bayesian Optimisation of Structured Spaces. ICML 2025, PMLR 267:44956-44970; Sections 4-5 describe the anchor.
